subject: Runway preflight: infra levers, capacity readiness, and unit-econ scenarios
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-03T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Runway preflight: infra levers & unit-econ scenarios

Team —

QBR is next Wednesday; I need a short, actionable preflight packet focused on the Atlas Retail deal and our broader runway assumptions. Specifically:

- Current committed GPU capacity vs expected 90/95/99 pctile demand over next 6 months (by model family).
- Per-token unit econ projections for hosted vs dedicated (simple table: cost/token, latency band, recommended routing).
- Sensitivity scenarios for batching and KV-prefix caching on small/medium/large sessions (p90 latency and cost delta).
- Any near-term supply constraints (spot interruptions, region-specific capacity) and mitigation levers.

I've attached a working workbook (qbr_runway_model_v3.xlsx) — fill the "Ops Inputs" tab with numbers and add a one-paragraph recommendation. Keep it short: 1 slide + 1 page.

Deadline: EOD Monday (10/4) so I can synthesize for exec prep.

Tessa
--
Tessa Morgan
Head of Platforms, Redwood Inference
T: 415-555-0182

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-03T12:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runway preflight: infra levers & unit-econ scenarios

Thanks — attaching my draft numbers (Ops Inputs tab filled). Key takeaways at a glance:

- Committed GPU pool usage today: 67% avg; projected to 78% in 6 weeks with current ramp.
- If we convert 20% of high-latency users to a cached path, unit cost drops ~12% for that cohort.
- Dedicated pricing still favorable for Atlas' committed throughput; propose reserved 6-month slots + burst.

Open questions for Vivek: I left a note in the sheet about batching assumptions for the small-session distribution (session length < 32 tokens). If caching works as modeled we should see minimal p95 regression.

Attachments: qbr_runway_model_v3.xlsx

-Lauren
--
Lauren Bishop
VP, Infrastructure Strategy

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runway preflight: infra levers & unit-econ scenarios

Quick technical notes based on Lauren's inputs and our sim runs:

- Batching assumptions: current model assumes up to 1.8x effective throughput for long-sequence workloads when burst windows align. For short sessions (<32 tokens) batching helps less (1.1x); that's where KV prefix caching buys the most.
- Cache hit model: a 30% cache hit on prefixes reduces token compute by ~20% overall (depends on distribution). See attached sim PDF with p90/p95 deltas.
- Latency tradeoffs: aggressive batch windows (>50ms) lower cost but push p95 for interactive customers beyond 350ms; recommend tiered policy by customer SLA.
- Spot risk: one provider in eu-central shows higher preemption rates in our test region; recommend avoiding immediate region failover for Atlas (they have eu presence).

Attaching: batch_cache_simulations.pdf (contains charts and p95 tables).

-Vivek
--
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@atlasretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-05T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runway preflight: infra levers & unit-econ scenarios

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from procurement/ops at Atlas:

- Can you confirm the proposed dedicated pricing for 6-month reserved slots vs. on-demand per-token today (we need a clear delta for our CFO)?
- We're sensitive to p95 latency for agent flows; what's your recommended SLA/route for our cohort to keep p95 under 300ms?
- Last: can you include a short paragraph on fallback behavior during region capacity loss (we need to know whether multi-region failover or model fallback is expected).

If possible, please add a one-pager we can share with our procurement team.

Best,
Olivia Chen
Head of Platform Ops, Atlas Retail
procure@atlasretail.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@atlasretail.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-05T16:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runway preflight: infra levers & unit-econ scenarios

Olivia — thanks, good questions. Short answers below; I'll attach the one-pager to the deliverable we share tomorrow: 

1) Pricing delta: Lauren's workbook includes a pricing comparison table (Hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved 6-month slots). Net: dedicated reserved slots are ~28% cheaper at Atlas' committed throughput (assumes 60% utilization baseline). We'll add a CFO-friendly summary line.

2) SLA recommendation: For p95 < 300ms on agent flows we recommend routing Atlas to our dedicated pool in us-west (p95 measured at ~270ms with current model mix) plus KV-prefix caching for agent prompts. If the customer requires global routing, add regional dedicated pools or model-fallback (quantized variant) as backup — that increases predicted unit cost by ~8%.

3) Failover behavior: Primary recommendation is model fallback (quantized model variant) + routing to a dedicated pool in a secondary region. Multi-region live failover is higher cost and has longer failover time; we'll document the tradeoffs in the one-pager.

Action items (who/when):
- Lauren: finalize CFO pricing summary (EOD 10/5).
- Vivek: add a 2-line failover runbook and an annotated p95 table in the sim PDF (EOD 10/5).
- Tessa: synthesize one-pager and slide for exec (10/6 morning).

I'll share the consolidated packet with Atlas and execs tomorrow morning.

Thanks all,
Tessa
--
Tessa Morgan
Head of Platforms, Redwood Inference
